page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware maps 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 16.0 GB, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per socket structure. The instance lacks bundled GPUs and includes no local ephemeral SSD storage, relying on external network storage options.

In benchmark testing, the n2d-standard-4 demonstrates strong single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% of evaluated cloud hardware at 2688.38 operations per second. Multi-core performance metrics show lower resource density scaling, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores landing in the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests yield mid-tier performance for large-block uncached read and write operations at 44.77 GB/sec and 35.36 GB/sec respectively, whereas small-block cached memory bandwidth remains in the lower quartile. Cryptographic operations show stable throughput backed by hardware AES, VAES, and SHA extensions.

Given its hardware composition and performance profile, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for light general computing requirements where peak multi-threaded scaling is not critical. It is well suited for entry-level web serving, lightweight microservices, basic CI/CD build agents, utility background processing, and low-concurrency application backends.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose instance driven by a 64-bit AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a 4.0 GB per vCPU memory balance. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache, operates without bundled GPUs, and relies entirely on remote storage solution options as no local storage is attached. In performance testing, single-threaded CPU execution shows notable relative strength, achieving a top-quartile stress-ng single-core benchmark. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU output and memory access patterns fall within lower performance bands, as evidenced by bottom-quartile PassMark CPU and multi-core Geekbench results. The overall technical profile makes n2d-standard-4 a cost-effective choice for light application backends, basic web serving, utility workers, and general operational workloads that do not demand heavy concurrent execution.
